Nigeria Democratic Congress Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, has mourned former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, describing him as an elder brother with whom he shared a cordial working relationship. In a condolence message posted on his X handle on Tuesday, Obi expressed his grief, while recalling their collaboration in advocating for the award of the contract for the Second Niger Bridge. He wrote, “I am deeply saddened by the passing of my very dear elder brother, His Excellency, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, former Governor of Delta State. In my interactions with him, he treated me like his junior brother.” Obi said he fondly remembered their working relationship while they were both in public service, particularly their joint efforts to advance the Second Niger Bridge project. He added, “I recall with fondness the cordial working relationship I enjoyed with him during our time in public service. We worked together as brothers in the collective effort to promote and advocate for the award of the contract for the Second Niger Bridge, recognising its importance to national integration, commerce, and the development of the South-East and South-South.” Uduaghan’s legacy will endure, Delta NDC gov candidate mourns Morning recap: NLC ultimatum heightens FG tension, Tinubu defends subsidy removal, other top stories I never asked Nigerians abroad to abandon families — Obi The former Anambra State governor expressed satisfaction that their efforts eventually yielded results, with the bridge becoming a reality. Obi described Uduaghan’s death as a loss to his family, Delta State and the country. “His passing is a loss to his family, the people of Delta State, and our nation,” he said. He extended his condolences to the late governor’s family, the Delta State Government and the people of the state, while praying for God to grant him eternal rest and comfort those mourning him.
